controls.basis: a relative difference of 0.5 against a tolerance of 1e-12 is arithmetic
controls.control: a real numeric difference exceeds the tolerance

controls.basis: a value equals itself; zero follows by arithmetic

instrument_controls.does_not_establish: that the instrument's other measurements are correct. A control pair shows it still responds to a known stimulus and stays silent on a null one -- it is a liveness and discrimination check, not a calibration.

note: Bit identity is NOT demanded where the platform contract does not guarantee it. The four outcomes are reported separately so a numerical difference is never read as a decision failure, and a decision failure is never excused as rounding.

runs.fidelity_note: The hand-off reconstruction now keys on channel ARRIVAL TIME, which is what the live adapter's freshness gate does. The earlier reconstruction compared VALUES and so missed 58.8% of hand-offs on a committed log, because two identical consecutive readings looked like no new reading (HF-010). That removed most of the ArduPilot divergence -- 511 categorical differences fell to 13 -- and left PX4 unchanged at 144, so what remains on PX4 has a DIFFERENT cause. HF-014 has now attributed the MECHANISM and not the root cause: all 144 are the replay seeing MORE live edges than the recording (never fewer), 122 of them exactly `altitude_baro`, and every affected edge is one whose weight is a product of per-sensor FRESHNESS terms while the residual values agree. A single differing staleness timeout was tested as the explanation and RULED OUT. Why the live side differed cannot be settled from these logs, which never recorded the layer's own `fresh` map; logs written after HF-014 do. THE VERDICT IS STILL DIVERGENT ON BOTH PLATFORMS: decision replay does not yet serve as a verification instrument, and the software-hardening gate must not count it as PASS.
